title: esc_ui B1 pin cannot fire the demolish: the hook only handles Junction selections but the scenario selects a router
evidence:
+parity_ui_press_effect :: proc(user: rawptr, ictx: ^inp.Input, pos: rl.Vector2) -> bool {
+	if ictx.sel_node >= 0 {
+		slot, ok := pp.node_slot(ictx.topo, u32(ictx.sel_node))
+		if ok && ictx.topo.node_kind[slot] == .Junction {
...
+			evs(inp.Mouse_Press{pos = n1, button = .Left}), // select the router
...
+// parity_ui_press_effect — the app's popover_click demolish-button path, wired
+// into the parity ctx so the B1 pin (same-frame ESC + UI click) exercises the
+// UI-swallow surface: a press on the selected junction's demolish button
+// swallows + fires the demolish through the shared executor.
detail: The hook gates the demolish on node_kind == .Junction, but the scenario selects 'the router' at n1 (demolish_btn_center anchors at FIXTURE_RT_POS). The demolish can never fire, so the empty-command assert passes even if the map-time deselect fix is reverted.
recommended_fix: Select a fixture Junction for the B1 pin (or drop the kind gate), so a live selection can actually reach inp.demolish_node; otherwise the pin never discriminates.

title: esc_pressed is written but never read; drag suppression gates on esc_cancelled only, so ESC on the deselect path still takes the drag branch
evidence:
+	esc_pressed := false // any ESC key this frame
...
+	if has_key(keys[:], .Esc) {
+		esc_pressed = true
+	}
...
+	drag_eff := inp.drag.active && !esc_cancelled
detail: esc_pressed is set once and never consumed anywhere in the delta — dead. esc_cancelled is only true when placing >= 0, so a same-frame ESC on the deselect path (placing < 0) with a live draw drag still enters the drag branch; the B2 no-op suppression is asymmetric.
recommended_fix: Either use esc_pressed ('any ESC this frame') in drag_eff so both ESC branches suppress the stale-drag branch, or delete it; add a placing<0 ESC+release scenario if that case must also be a no-op.

title: ESC-branch edit misindents esc_cancelled = true and the new '} else {' line
detail: The replacement dedents esc_cancelled = true to the if's level and leaves '} else {' misaligned. Odin ignores indentation so it compiles, but the hunk breaks the surrounding block style for no reason.
recommended_fix: Re-indent to match the surrounding blocks: esc_cancelled = true one level under the if, and '} else {' aligned with the if.

title: !esc_cancelled in the chord guard is redundant: esc_cancelled forces placing_eff = -1 above
detail: Since esc_cancelled immediately forces placing_eff = -1, the condition placing_eff >= 0 already implies !esc_cancelled; the extra conjunct adds nothing and muddies which queued Cancel the comment is gating on.
recommended_fix: Drop '&& !esc_cancelled' and adjust the comment to name the actual cancel being gated (the left-press placement cancel), or keep it only if it guards a distinct future state.
